732201101.text: Wow... Paimon didn't think that a place like this could exist in the desert...

732201102.text: Huh? Was the sun already going down when we first came out from underground?

732201103.text: No... This is my mistress' paradise, a place frozen at the point where the sky kisses the waters, where ingenuity and devotion comingle. The resultant here and now, then, is named eternity.

732201104.text: Wow... Paimon understood almost none of that, but it's why nothing moves here, right?

732201105.text: Is this why my parents regarded this place as their final destination?

732201106.text: Those are not my words... *sigh* Interpret this however you will, poor child...

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to where the Goddess of Flowers slumbers

732201201.text: My mistress... She is not here.

732201202.text: Instead, here is another fragment of myself...

732201301.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away... But a warmth then quickly fills you.

732201302.text:
Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you see a palace shaped by bricks of crimson jade bound to a garden, flourishing with a multiplicity of vibrant plants that bask in infinite bird-song.
The Jinn are the most intelligent servants of the Mistress of Flowers, and to her they are minstrels and cupbearers both.
In her garden, addled monks and ragged wanderers dance, spiraling in step with the daffodils, supping the lifeblood of the daughters of the vine...
Here is a garden unlike any other, the place where the Lord of Flowers once lived, the place where she now sleeps...

732201303.text: "The roses blossom like crackling flames, setting the lives of nocturnal birds aflame. And though the candles smile gently, they offer the approaching moths only ruin."

732201304.text: You see her reach out and behold her skin gleaming with lunar sheen. You gaze upon her mien and witness ineffable beauty. Her appearance is like the totality of her Jinn, their wondrous aspects only mere petals to her complete flower, her being the quintessence to every last scent in existence...\nAnd then, you meet her gaze—

732201305.text: And face nothingness.\nYou greet the endless void, falling into its embrace, mind afire with constant terror...

732201306.text: As your consciousness clears, you find Jeht clutching your hand, her expression clouded with concern.

732201307.text: You're awake... How are you feeling?

732201308.text: You just... *sigh* Never mind. The important thing is that you're alright...

732201309.text: What... What did you see? You look like you just woke up from a long and scary dream...

732201313.text: She is gone. He lied to us. He lied to us all.

732201315.text: It's nothing — just the cancellation of an ancient pact. I believe I'm... finally free?

732201316.text: The Lord of the Sands once swore to us that our Mistress of Flowers slumbered here, destined to awake someday. But...

732201317.text: How strange. Our mistress has already passed. He... He deceived me. He deceived my people.

732201318.text: I should feel maddening hatred for him right now. For this desert. For the death of my mistress... My loathing should have matched the love and admiration I once held for him...

732201319.text: Yet, I find myself empty of want or will to hate... How odd...

732201402.text: This place should be it... It matches the sketches in my mother's journal.

732201403.text: A fine place for a restful slumber, no?

732201405.text: We've faced countless dangers in our trek across this desert: betrayals, plots... Unforgivable wrongs, incomprehensible events... All in quick succession too...

732201406.text: But here, I feel calm... Happy. I don't know why. I just do.

732201407.text: It is because this place is the Mistress of Flowers' final sphere of influence... The offerings of the skies protect its serenity here, deep beneath the earth. Thus does this place preserve the last of her essence...

732201408.text: And though she is long gone, this place remains as calm as it was at its inception, as if it was never disturbed. Hence, those who arrive in this place... will know only peace and joy.

732201409.text: For the mistress was once the guardian of maddened monks and lost wanderers. To them, this place was indeed a paradise they could call home.

732201411.text: Jeht quietly sets her mother's notes down and lays Jebrael's axe by its side...\nNow, it is as if they were never parted.

732200601.text: Sorry... I'm just at a loss for words right now.

732200602.text: It's like... time forgot how to flow and everything stopped. I don't know why. I can't even gasp in astonishment at all that's around me here because... All I feel is peace.

732200603.text: For my parents to slumber here alongside our fallen goddess... Though I wish they had never left...

732200604.text: I truly wish that they could stay here eternally, never to be forgotten by the passing of time.

732200606.text: When we first entered, we disrupted the fragment's power and broke the device that long maintained equilibrium here... This place is destined for ruin, to be swallowed by the sands sooner or later.

732200607.text: When that time comes, the fading power that our mistress put forth to ward this oasis in perpetuity will dissipate... This is inevitable.

732200608.text: I know that. But at least my parents were reunited before the end, as if they'd never left each other at all.

732200609.text: Maybe there will finally come a day when I return to this place. After I grow weary of adventuring, and after I have left every place I regard to be "home" behind.

732200610.text: At that point, I think I'll just say: "I'm back!" and then lay between my parents to join them for a grand old nap.

732200612.text: Jeht... But that day's still far, far away! Right now Jebrael is probably happily... um, not-smiling, because his face is always blank. But Paimon's sure he's happy...

732200614.text: #And you too, {NICKNAME}. Thanks for walking this path with me, and for fulfilling this willful, cherished desire of mine... But I'd like to have a bit of alone-time with my parents...

732200618.text: Don't worry about me... I'll catch up. Ha. I mean, it isn't my time to settle down here yet, is it?

732201801.text: She is a good child, my master.

732201802.text: Though born to beastly brutality and slight of wit, her survival instincts are astute beyond compare...

732201803.text: She perceives who it is who wishes to see her hurt, and upon sensing such intent, she gives her all to retaliate without mercy, regardless of how much intimacy may lie between...

732201804.text: Still... She does not know the schemes woven against her. She does not yet know that the home she seeks... is a thing most hollow.

732201805.text: Master, if you care for her, then protect her well.

732201806.text: A mere suggestion on my part, of course. You may take it to be... I do not know. Perhaps you might consider it the unworthy atonement of one who was once a mother...

732201502.text: (There she sits in silence, enjoying a pleasant time with her parents.)

732201506.text: If you don't mind, I'd like to stay a while longer... If that's okay with you, I mean.

732201601.text: I feel much better now. Thanks.

732201602.text: Are you sure you're fine? You can rest more if you want...

732201603.text: Let's head back. We need to tell Matriarch Babel about the details of our journey.

732201604.text: Alright, if you say so... Then, let's go!

732200801.text: We're back and intact, Matriarch Babel.

732200802.text: We have discovered the secrets of the Eternal Oasis, and opened the path there for the tribe.

732200803.text: I... Thank you for this opportunity. To help me fulfill my parents' dreams... Even if they didn't receive the blessings of the Tanit.

732200804.text: Please, child, there's no need. I have always held your hopes close to my heart. To be able to fulfill the desires of the young is my duty as Matriarch.

732200806.text: Well done, Jeht. Now, there is the matter of Azariq...

732200807.text: Your judgment was accurate... He's undoubtedly a traitor.

732200808.text: Wait, so you already knew that Azariq would betray you?

732200809.text: No. I only suspected him at first, and spent most of the journey watching him... I just didn't expect him to reveal his true intent so soon.

732200810.text: Matriarch Babel warned me, but I chose to believe him at the time.

732200811.text: Here: proof of his collusion with the Fatui.

732200812.text: Jeht gives Aderfi's letter to Babel.

732200814.text: Please don't be sad, Matriarch Babel...

732200815.text: Yes... I long-suspected his disloyalty. It is just a shame that I didn't get the chance to end him personally... And I had such high hopes for him, too.

732200816.text: But now, with the tribe facing increasingly treacherous circumstances, and the loss of two individuals I invested much time and effort in, I must count on you, Jeht, to help me in matters both great and small going forward.

732200817.text: So... What you're saying is that Jeht got a promotion? Yeah! Congratulations, Jeht!

732200818.text: Promotion? Haha... That's not a word you hear in the desert very often.

732200819.text: We desert-dwellers aren't so hierarchical. In the end, they who govern more affairs will be the ones to bear greater authority.

732200820.text: Jeht... The future of the Tanit now rests on your shoulders. Don't let the tribe down.

732200821.text: Tribe... So, you're saying I'm truly one of the Tanit now?

732200822.text: Do not be deceived, child. I have always seen you as one of us. Whatever happened before, you are a daughter of the Tanit, and the truth of our consanguinity will always run in your veins.

732200824.text: Hmm, Paimon feels like we've forgotten to mention some suspicious things we saw...

732200825.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you remember seeing anything suspicious?

732200827.text: You once dispatched other tribespeople into the oasis and left them to perish there. Then, you laid a taboo upon it as a pretext to prevent anyone else from trespassing, did you not?

732200828.text: Yet, you encouraged us to head deeper into that same treacherous territory, mentioning nothing of your actions. Why did you do this?

732200831.text: Esteemed Liloupar, allow me to offer my deepest apologies for all the inconveniences and misunderstandings you must have experienced.

732200832.text: But you are right. We have been exploring the ruins of Gurabad and the Eternal Oasis for quite some time... I sent many people from the tribe there in times past.

732200833.text: That we learned these few key locations and the general layout of the area is all thanks to their efforts...

732200834.text: Yet, due to the extreme danger of the missions, a vast majority of those brave explorers never returned, and the efforts from these expeditions bore scarce fruit.

732200835.text: Hence, I put a stop to the forays and marked entry into the place as taboo.

732200836.text: The traitor, Azariq, once led teams to survey the canyon and the ruins, and so I thought I could trust him to serve as your guide. I did not initially think that he would turn on us...

732200838.text: Because I knew from the start that you would return unharmed. Of all who inherit our legacy, you are the one I trust the most, Jeht.

732200839.text: Your fearlessness, your fierceness, your cunning, along with the gentleness and sincerity with which you treat your tribe and friends... They have not gone unnoticed.

732200840.text: If my daughter had not been stolen from me by the sands, I like to think that she might've turned out to be like you. Unflinching in the face of all peril, one whom even the desert could not smother...

732200841.text: So I believed in you and prayed for you in silence.

732200843.text: ...I'm sorry for doubting you, Matriarch Babel.

732200844.text: No. The fault is mine for incurring your doubt and mistrust. It is I who should ask for forgiveness instead.

732200865.text: My apologies as well, my master. It seems that my paranoia got the best of me.

732200866.text: #Well, it is good that we all managed to clear the air between us. You are our honored guest, {NICKNAME}, and the Tanit will always welcome you.

732200867.text: Esteemed Master of the Jinni, whatever you may desire, I will do my utmost to fulfill, if you would only ask.

732200846.text: In Azariq and Aderfi's correspondence, it was mentioned that the reason they turned traitor was because you showed favoritism toward Jeht, who is a traitor's daughter in their eyes, and wanted her to serve as inheritor to your duties...

732200848.text: Aside from that, you also seem to be actively culling those who work with those you call the "northerners." Yet, you once relied on these very same traitors to strike deals with said northerners.

732200849.text: Now, the jargon of your people eludes my understanding, but I am curious as to what the words you just spoke meant.

732200851.text: Esteemed Liloupar, allow me to offer my deepest apologies for all the inconveniences and misunderstandings you must have experienced.

732200852.text: But the survival and prosperity of the Tanit can only be sustained through multilateral trade. That includes those who hail from the north.

732200853.text: Preoccupied as I was by a multitude of matters surrounding the tribe, I was unable to foresee the treachery these northerners harbored...

732200854.text: Later, I would discover that the dangers they represented far outweighed the benefits they offered... But by then, I could only take to removing the traitors within our tribe that had turned to them first.

732200855.text: This is also why I needed Jeht. Her ability to swiftly and efficiently cleanse the tribe of traitors is unmatched. Additionally, I deeply appreciate her loyalty and capability.

732200857.text: Because I knew from the start that you would return unharmed. Of all who inherit our legacy, you are the one I trust the most, Jeht.

732200858.text: Your fearlessness, your fierceness, your cunning, along with the gentleness and sincerity with which you treat your tribe and friends... They have not gone unnoticed.

732200859.text: If my daughter had not been stolen from me by the sands, I like to think that she might've turned out to be like you. Unflinching in the face of all peril, one whom even the desert could not smother...

732200860.text: So I believed in you and prayed for you in silence.

732200862.text: ...I'm sorry for doubting you, Matriarch Babel.

732200863.text: No. The fault is mine for incurring your doubt and mistrust. It is I who should ask for forgiveness instead.

732205002.text: (There she sits in silence, enjoying a pleasant time with her parents.)

732209904.text: After pacing for a while, you decide to leave this oasis of stillness.\nSoon, Jeht catches up with you.
